finding.claim: Keys added with a Confirm constraint (ssh-add -c) are signed without any confirmation. try_sign never calls the Agent::confirm hook; it hardcodes ok=true, so the constraint is a no-op.
finding.source: Any client that can write frames to the agent socket: a SIGN request (msg 13) naming a key whose constraints contain CONSTRAIN_CONFIRM.
finding.sink: sign_with_hash_alg over the stored private key (server.rs:355).

trace.note: respond(): SIGN arm guard is !is_locked && agentref.confirm_request(Sign); confirm_request defaults to true (line 57-59).
agent taken, then try_sign(agent, r, writebuf) called.
Looks up key blob in KeyStore; constraints destructured.
needs_confirm = true when constraints contain Constraint::Confirm.
needs_confirm branch: the Agent::confirm(self, key) hook (trait lines 50-55, 86-88) is never invoked.
ok is set to literal true inside a futures::future::ready((agent, true)) block; the pending confirmation never happens.
Signature produced and returned to the client.

finding.guards_checked: is_locked check (server.rs:131-137); confirm_request gate (default true, trait line 57); constraint parsing in add_key (lines 286-312) correctly records Confirm; lookup miss returns FAILURE (line 336). None of these prompt the user. Caveat: the trait default confirm() also returns true, so the library itself gives no confirmation, and any implementer relying on the hook gets none.

finding.claim: Config::max_auth_attempts is documented as the maximum number of authentication attempts but is never read. rejection_count is incremented and never compared, so a single connection can retry authentication without limit.
finding.source: Unauthenticated remote client sending repeated SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_REQUEST (password / publickey / none).
finding.sink: Handler::auth_password (encrypted.rs:562) and Handler::auth_publickey (encrypted.rs:779), i.e. credential checks on attacker-chosen input.

trace.note: max_auth_attempts field documented as 'Maximal number of allowed authentication attempts'.
Default max_auth_attempts = 10.
method == password branch: no attempt count check.
handler.auth_password called on attacker-supplied password.
Rejection path: reject_auth_request.
rejection_count += 1 with no comparison against config.max_auth_attempts; grep finds no read of max_auth_attempts outside the config struct.
Only throttle: tokio::time::sleep_until(until), about 1s per attempt (auth_rejection_time default at server/mod.rs:112).

finding.guards_checked: auth_rejection_time sleep (encrypted.rs:882) limits rate to about 1 attempt/s per connection. inactivity_timeout (default 600s, mod.rs:122) bounds connection lifetime, not attempts. Nothing disconnects after N failures. Severity depends on how much the application's auth_password/auth_publickey relies on the library for brute-force protection.

finding.claim: The server never checks the client-selected auth method against the advertised/allowed auth_request.methods set. Config::methods only controls the list advertised to the client, so a method the server meant to disable still reaches its handler.
finding.source: Client-chosen method name in USERAUTH_REQUEST: password (541), publickey (583), none (593), keyboard-interactive (624).
finding.sink: Handler::auth_password / auth_publickey / auth_none / auth_keyboard_interactive, which can return Accept.

trace.note: Config::methods documented as 'Authentication methods proposed to the client' (advisory).
config methods used only to build the initial AuthRequest for advertisement.
password branch dispatches without checking auth_request.methods contains Password.
handler.auth_password invoked; Accept leads to InitCompression (line 566).
proceed_with_methods overwrites the list only on reject; never used to gate incoming requests.

finding.guards_checked: Handler-level checks only. grep finds no methods.contains / membership test on the incoming path (encrypted.rs references at 574-618, 795, 843 only write the list). Defense-in-depth gap: a publickey-only server still runs password handler code if the client asks for it.

finding.claim: Server-side certificate auth checks only validity window and self-signature. It does not check that the signing CA is trusted, that cert_type is User, or that valid_principals contains the requested user. Those checks fall entirely to the handler, and the trait docs do not say so.
finding.source: Remote client presenting an OpenSSH certificate signed by an attacker-controlled CA with the attacker's own key.
finding.sink: Handler::auth_openssh_certificate (encrypted.rs:782), the authorization decision for certificate logins.

trace.note: PublicKeyOrCertificate::Certificate branch.
valid_after / valid_before checked against SystemTime::now().
cert.verify_signature(): verifies the cert against its own embedded signature_key, so any self-made CA passes.
pubkey = cert.public_key() used for signature check (763-774).
Signature over session id + request verified with cert's subject key.
handler.auth_openssh_certificate(user, cert) called; no CA, principal or cert-type check precedes it.
Default implementation returns Auth::reject(), so the default configuration is safe; the risk exists only where the handler accepts.

finding.guards_checked: expiry window (encrypted.rs:702-711); self-signature (714); subject-key possession proof (774); default handler reject (server/mod.rs:296). Not checked by the library: CA trust, cert type, principals, critical options (force-command, source-address). Plausible as a footgun; exploitable only if an application's handler accepts certificates after these checks are skipped.

finding.claim: For a constrained add with an unknown constraint byte, the agent sends SUCCESS and then FAILURE in one frame, and the key is not stored. The client reads the leading SUCCESS and believes the key was added.
finding.source: Local client sending SSH_AGENTC_ADD_ID_CONSTRAINED (msg 25) with an unrecognized constraint type byte.
finding.sink: Agent response frame (writebuf) returned to the client.

trace.note: Constrained add arm calls add_key(r, true, writebuf).
writebuf.push(SUCCESS) happens before constraint parsing.
Unknown constraint byte falls into the else branch.
return Ok(false) before w.insert, so the key is not stored.
respond(): Ok(false) is not Ok(true), so FAILURE is pushed after SUCCESS (line 227).
Length header = 2 covering [SUCCESS, FAILURE]; the client reads SUCCESS and the stray FAILURE byte desynchronises the stream.

finding.guards_checked: Stored key is not inserted (no key-state corruption). Impact is a misleading success report and a desynced stream for the same local client. Low severity.

finding.claim: Lock with an empty password reports SUCCESS but leaves the agent unlocked, because is_locked is defined as lock-password non-empty.
finding.source: Local client sending SSH_AGENTC_LOCK (msg 22) with a zero-length password.
finding.sink: Lock state; the client believes the agent is locked.

trace.note: Lock arm guarded by !is_locked.
self.lock(&mut r) returns Ok.
lock.extend(empty) leaves lock empty.
SUCCESS returned; is_locked remains false (line 133), so signing and listing still work.

finding.guards_checked: No check that the lock password is non-empty. Low severity; relevant to users who depend on lock as a hard stop.

finding.claim: Agent unlock compares the stored lock password to the supplied one with slice equality, which short-circuits on the first differing byte.
finding.source: Local client sending SSH_AGENTC_UNLOCK (msg 23) with guessed passwords.
finding.sink: Lock check guarding unlock of stored keys.

trace.note: Unlock arm guarded by is_locked and confirm_request(Unlock).
unlock() decodes password.
lock[..] == password is a short-circuit comparison.

finding.guards_checked: Per-connection frame cap (server.rs:108); unlock is the only path that clears the lock; no rate limit on unlock attempts. Low severity: local attacker only, timing side channel over a local socket is hard to exploit.

finding.claim: If a client explicitly includes the 'none' KEX in its preferences and the server selects it, the handshake returns with server_host_key = None, which skips the client's check_server_key and any signature check.
finding.source: Server-selected KEX name 'none', only possible when the client's own Preferred.kex includes NONE.
finding.sink: Session establishment without host authentication (client/mod.rs:1682-1687 skipped).

trace.note: Non-standard no-kex exchange branch.
compute_keys with empty shared secret.
Returns KexProgress::Done with server_host_key: None, before any exchange-hash signature verification (lines 287-298 are not reached).
if let Some(server_host_key) guards check_server_key; None means no check.

finding.guards_checked: Default Preferred (negotiation.rs:105-119) excludes kex::NONE, so default clients are not affected. Opt-in footgun only; should be refused or require explicit acknowledgement.

finding.claim: learn_known_hosts_path writes the host argument into known_hosts without validating it, so a host string containing a newline or space can inject extra known_hosts lines, including a trusted key for another host.
finding.source: A hostname string from an untrusted source passed to learn_known_hosts (caller-supplied; not network-controlled inside this library).
finding.sink: Append to the user's known_hosts file (known_hosts.rs:150-172).

trace.note: learn_known_hosts(host, port, pubkey) public entry point; no validation of host.
File opened in append mode.
write!(file, "[{host}]:{port} ") when port != 22.
write!(file, "{host} ") when port == 22; host embedded raw.
Attacker-chosen key appended after the injected host field.

finding.guards_checked: check_known_hosts_path fails closed on key mismatch (known_hosts.rs:38), and match_hostname uses exact matching, so the injection only matters if a crafted hostname is later learned. Only reachable when the caller passes untrusted host strings. Low severity; treat as hardening.
